questions.question: According to the framework presented in Table 3.1, which of the following is NOT one of the four general moral principles that apply to scientific research?

answers.text: Weighing risks against benefits
Maximizing financial compensation
Seeking justice
Respecting people's rights and dignity

questions.question: In Milgram's obedience study, what was the primary ethical concern regarding the research participants?

answers.text: They were not compensated adequately for their time
They experienced severe psychological stress during the procedure
They were denied access to the study results
They were required to participate against their will

questions.question: The Tuskegee syphilis study is primarily an example of a violation of which moral principle?

answers.text: Acting responsibly and with integrity
Seeking justice
Weighing risks against benefits
Minimizing deception

questions.question: According to the chapter, what did participants in the Tuskegee study believe they were receiving?

answers.text: Experimental treatment for heart disease
Treatment for 'bad blood'
A new vaccine for syphilis
Routine health screenings only

questions.question: Which ethics code was written in 1947 in conjunction with the trials of Nazi physicians?

answers.text: The Declaration of Helsinki
The Belmont Report
The Nuremberg Code
The APA Ethics Code

questions.question: What year was the Belmont Report published?
According to the chapter, an institutional review board (IRB) must consist of at least how many people?

answers.text: Three
Five
Seven
Ten

questions.question: Which level of research risk is the lowest and includes studies on the effectiveness of normal educational activities?

answers.text: Minimal risk research
Expedited research
Exempt research
Greater than minimal risk research

questions.question: According to APA Ethics Code Standard 8.02, informed consent must include information about all of the following EXCEPT:

answers.text: The purpose of the research and expected duration
The researcher's personal beliefs about the topic
Participants' right to decline or withdraw
Limits of confidentiality

questions.question: What does the chapter define as 'anonymity' in research?

answers.text: When researchers agree not to disclose participants' information
When participants' names and personally identifiable information are not collected at all
When data is stored in a locked cabinet
When participants use pseudonyms during the study

questions.question: In the 'personal space' study conducted in a public men's room, what did researchers secretly observe?

answers.text: How long participants washed their hands
Whether it took participants longer to begin urinating when another man was nearby
How participants reacted to crowded conditions
Whether participants maintained eye contact with confederates

questions.question: According to APA Standard 8.07, under what condition is deception NOT allowed in research?

answers.text: When effective nondeceptive alternatives are available
When the research is reasonably expected to cause physical pain or severe emotional distress
When participants cannot be debriefed immediately
When the study involves minimal risk

questions.question: What is debriefing?

answers.text: The initial screening process to determine participant eligibility
The process of informing participants of the study's purpose and revealing any deception as soon as possible
The payment procedure at the end of the study
The confidentiality agreement signed before participation

questions.question: In Jerry Burger's 2009 replication of Milgram's study, what modification was made to minimize risks?

answers.text: Participants were told the shocks were fake before the study began
The procedure was always stopped when participants were about to administer the 150-V shock
No confederates were used in the study
Participants were allowed to leave at any time without consequences

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is 'self-plagiarism'?

answers.text: Using your own ideas without proper documentation
Publishing the same material more than once
Citing yourself too frequently in a paper
Reusing old data in a new study

questions.question: When President Bill Clinton apologized for the Tuskegee study in 1997, how many years had passed since the study began?

answers.text: 25 years
40 years
65 years
75 years

questions.question: According to APA Standard 8.10, what must psychologists do if they discover significant errors in their published data?

answers.text: Ignore minor errors and only correct major ones
Take reasonable steps to correct such errors through a correction, retraction, erratum, or other appropriate means
Withdraw from future research in that area
Notify only the journal editor privately

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of deception that does NOT involve actively misleading participants?

answers.text: Using a confederate who pretends to be another participant
Withholding information about the full design or true purpose of the study
Providing false feedback about performance
Using phony equipment like a fake shock generator

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is one criticism of how Milgram handled the ethical issues in his obedience study?

answers.text: He did not obtain institutional approval before conducting the research
Although he did not know participants would react severely initially, he should have made adjustments after testing the first several participants
He failed to compensate participants for their time
He did not use a proper control group

questions.question: According to APA Standard 8.12b on publication credit, under what circumstance should a student be listed as principal author?

answers.text: Only if the student collected all the data personally
When a multiple-authored article is substantially based on the student's doctoral dissertation, except under exceptional circumstances
Only if the faculty advisor agrees to be listed as second author
Never, because faculty advisors must always be first author
